contract: A resized cover request writes the cache file <id>_<width>[x<height>].<format> under metadata/cache/covers with the requested dimensions, a repeated request serves the same bytes from that file, and a cover upload or selection purges the item's cache entries so the next request renders the new source. A multipart upload stores cover.<ext> with the uploaded bytes, removes older cover files only when their extension is in the allowlist (.jpeg, .jpg, .png, .webp, .jiff), keeps non-allowlisted files such as cover.svg, purges the item's cover cache, persists media.coverPath and item updatedAt, and emits item_updated after the commit. raw=1 serves the current stored cover file byte for byte with its image MIME type, Content-Length, Last-Modified and an ETag, answers 304 for a matching If-None-Match, and after a replacement serves the new bytes with a different ETag; a missing coverPath or file is 404. Deleting a cover answers 200, clears coverPath, purges the item's resized cache and makes raw and resized reads 404 without serving stale bytes; the cover file stays on disk as upstream leaves it. A cover url on a whitelisted loopback host stores the image bytes as cover.<ext> and sets coverPath; a literal private IPv4 destination that fails the SSRF filter answers 400 and leaves the previous coverPath, file and cache state unchanged. PATCH cover whose requested scanned library file is not a supported image answers 500 with the body 'Invalid image' and changes no coverPath, file or updatedAt. With EXP_PROXY_SUPPORT=1 upstream disables the SSRF filter but sets axios maxRedirects=0 and retries only 301/302: a cover url answering 307 answers 400 and leaves the previous coverPath, file and cache state unchanged. PATCH cover with a scanned image that differs from the stored coverPath copies it to metadata/items/<id>/cover.<ext>, removes older cover images, purges the resized cache, keeps unrelated files such as cover.svg, sets coverPath and emits item_updated; a same-path repeat copies again and emits again. When a multipart cover request carries both a url and a cover file the url takes precedence; an unsupported image signature at that url answers 400 without falling back to the uploaded file and leaves the item unchanged. PATCH cover accepts JSON bodies up to the 10 MB express.json limit: a 1.1 MB body is parsed and reaches the invalid-path 500 response, while a larger body is rejected with 413; neither changes the item.

invariants.contract: A resized cover request writes the cache file <id>_<width>[x<height>].<format> under metadata/cache/covers with the requested dimensions, a repeated request serves the same bytes from that file, and a cover upload or selection purges the item's cache entries so the next request renders the new source.

A multipart upload stores cover.<ext> with the uploaded bytes, removes older cover files only when their extension is in the allowlist (.jpeg, .jpg, .png, .webp, .jiff), keeps non-allowlisted files such as cover.svg, purges the item's cover cache, persists media.coverPath and item updatedAt, and emits item_updated after the commit.

raw=1 serves the current stored cover file byte for byte with its image MIME type, Content-Length, Last-Modified and an ETag, answers 304 for a matching If-None-Match, and after a replacement serves the new bytes with a different ETag; a missing coverPath or file is 404.
Deleting a cover answers 200, clears coverPath, purges the item's resized cache and makes raw and resized reads 404 without serving stale bytes; the cover file stays on disk as upstream leaves it.

A cover url on a whitelisted loopback host stores the image bytes as cover.<ext> and sets coverPath; a literal private IPv4 destination that fails the SSRF filter answers 400 and leaves the previous coverPath, file and cache state unchanged.
PATCH cover whose requested scanned library file is not a supported image answers 500 with the body 'Invalid image' and changes no coverPath, file or updatedAt.

With EXP_PROXY_SUPPORT=1 upstream disables the SSRF filter but sets axios maxRedirects=0 and retries only 301/302: a cover url answering 307 answers 400 and leaves the previous coverPath, file and cache state unchanged.

PATCH cover with a scanned image that differs from the stored coverPath copies it to metadata/items/<id>/cover.<ext>, removes older cover images, purges the resized cache, keeps unrelated files such as cover.svg, sets coverPath and emits item_updated; a same-path repeat copies again and emits again.

When a multipart cover request carries both a url and a cover file the url takes precedence; an unsupported image signature at that url answers 400 without falling back to the uploaded file and leaves the item unchanged.

PATCH cover accepts JSON bodies up to the 10 MB express.json limit: a 1.1 MB body is parsed and reaches the invalid-path 500 response, while a larger body is rejected with 413; neither changes the item.

evidence: go-backend/testmachine/contracts/parity/full-suite-report.json (2026-10-30: 101/101 HTTP cases; successful/repeated PATCH, Express response headers, stale-cache purge, allowlisted cleanup, multipart precedence, URL upload/failure, reads and delete lifecycle)
exceptions: force is not applicable: none of the cover routes has a force or override mode; a cover write simply replaces the previous cover.
All remote resources are loopback httptest servers (SSRF_REQUEST_FILTER_WHITELIST=127.0.0.1); no real internet host is used.
webp resizing is asserted as a produced WebP container with the FFmpeg build of the verification environment; exact encoder bytes are not pinned.
The X-Accel hand-off of the raw and cached covers is not asserted (no reverse proxy in the harness).
storeCoverWithItem=true (covers stored in the item folder) is not asserted here; the packet runs with the fixture default false.
